quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Before driving while taking any medicine, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor how the medicine will affect your driving.
Have someone follow you home.
Keep your window open and drive slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor how the medicine will affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Many medicines—both prescription and over-the-counter—can affect your ability to drive safely. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist about how any medicine might affect you. Be especially careful to ask about tranquilizers and sedatives.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: The right lane is ending. Merge left.
The road curves ahead.
There are intersections coming up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending. Merge left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions just ahead. This sign warns that one lane is ending and traffic must move to the left.

questions.question: Which statement about changing lanes is true?

options.text: Only turn and look over your right shoulder for both left and right lane changes.
Look over your right shoulder for right lane changes and your left shoulder for left lane changes.
Vehicles with two outside mirrors have no blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for right lane changes and your left shoulder for left lane changes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal and check all mirrors. Then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles are in the next lane.

questions.question: When driving through work zones, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Drive at your normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: In work zones, reduce your speed and stay alert. Follow posted speed limits. Workers may be present, so be prepared to stop at any time.

questions.question: When driving on slippery surfaces like snow or ice:

options.text: Use a low gear before going down steep hills.
Follow other vehicles closely to keep traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, shift to a low gear before driving downhill. Stay farther back from the car ahead than normal. Avoid quick stops. If you don't have antilock brakes, pump the brakes gently.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your lane.
Look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always check behind you before changing lanes. Look over your shoulder to make sure you won't hit anyone in the next lane. Also check that no one else is moving into that spot from another direction.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines mean:

options.text: No one can pass.
Both sides can pass.
The right lane can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left then right.
The road curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road will curve right, then curve left. Slow down and adjust your driving to handle these curves safely.

questions.question: You are on the freeway behind a large truck. You should drive:

options.text: Close behind the truck in bad weather so you can see farther ahead.
Farther back than you would behind a regular car.
Only one car length back so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther back than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely behind a truck, the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. Tailgating any vehicle is dangerous. Keep extra distance so you have room to stop if the truck stops suddenly.

questions.question: Remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You must see clearly through all your vehicle's windows. Clean all windows and mirrors of snow, ice, and frost before you drive.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the center means:

options.text: Slow down.
Traffic light ahead.
Do not pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: Solid yellow lines on two-lane roads mean you cannot pass. If one line is solid and one is broken, the driver on the solid line side cannot pass. Sometimes both lines are solid, meaning no one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving because:

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead because of darkness and glare from oncoming headlights. Always use your headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol can affect a driver's:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol can affect your ability to drive safely. Any alcohol can harm your judgment and coordination. Driving under the influence can lead to criminal charges.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
On the immediate left side of the cab.
On the immediate left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the immediate left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Trucks have much larger blind spots than cars. The driver cannot see a car directly behind them. If you drive too close behind a truck, you cannot see traffic ahead. If the driver cannot see your car in their side mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop before crossing.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait for a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down. Check for traffic crossing your path and then proceed carefully.

questions.question: When should you use your turn signal when parking next to a curb?

options.text: Only when pulling away from the curb.
When pulling next to the curb, but not when leaving.
When pulling next to the curb and when pulling away.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling next to the curb and when pulling away.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal both when you pull up to the curb and when you pull away from it.

questions.question: What should you do when driving at night?

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at oncoming headlights.
Keep more distance between your vehicle and the one ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep more distance between your vehicle and the one ahead.
questions.explanation: At night, increase your following distance because visibility is low. Use your headlights properly—use high beams only when appropriate. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights, as this causes glare and reduces your ability to see.

questions.question: You see one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line in the center of the road. The broken line is on your side. What does this mean?

options.text: You cannot pass in this area.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
You can only make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass. A solid line on the other side means oncoming traffic cannot pass. Always check for oncoming traffic before you pass.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits U-turns. You cannot turn around and go in the opposite direction where this sign is posted.

questions.question: When must you stop behind a school bus with flashing red lights?

options.text: Until all students are off the bus.
Until the stop arm is retracted.
Until the stop arm is retracted and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Until the stop arm is retracted and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: You must remain stopped until the red lights turn off, the stop arm folds in, and the bus begins to move.

questions.question: Before stopping at a traffic signal or sign, you should:

options.text: Press the accelerator hard.
Check your mirrors for traffic around you.
Set the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for traffic around you.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic. Be aware of other drivers as you slow down. Then move your foot to the brake and apply steady pressure for a smooth stop.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic, you should:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead of the gap.
Speed up and let other vehicles move out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead of the gap.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, check your mirrors and blind spots. Make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter.

questions.question: What does a red curb mean?

options.text: Loading zone.
The area is for picking up or dropping off passengers only.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: You cannot park, stand, or stop at a red curb.

questions.question: Which statement about braking and accelerating is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake abruptly to ensure you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both the brake and accelerator. Apply the brakes gently with steady pressure so your vehicle stops smoothly.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from the left.
You can pass from the right.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic is moving in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either side of the road.
